narrative.summary: On a transatlantic ocean liner, Neville Fairweather is found stabbed in his cabin. Passengers recall seeing him alive on the first-class promenade deck that evening. However, evidence reveals a crew member impersonated Neville to mislead witnesses. The detective, Katherine Bellamy, untangles the identity deception amidst rigid class segregation and shipboard procedures.

accepted_facts: Neville Fairweather was stabbed to death in his cabin between quarter past eight and quarter to nine.
Several first-class passengers saw Neville on the promenade deck around quarter to nine, dressed in a steward's uniform.
A torn piece of steward's uniform fabric was found snagged on Neville's cabin doorframe.
Crew schedules show Ferdinand Carrick was on duty in the first-class area during the time Neville was seen.
A first-class guest mentioned the steward appeared unusually nervous that evening.
The ship’s logbook shows Neville Fairweather signed for a late entry at the engine room shift change, but ink shades differ.
Ferdinand Carrick had opportunity and motive to impersonate Neville and commit the murder.
inferred_conclusions: The man seen on the promenade deck was Ferdinand Carrick disguised as Neville Fairweather.
The real Neville was already dead before the promenade sighting.
The forged engine room log entry was intended to create a false alibi.
Ferdinand Carrick’s nervousness and fabric evidence link him to the impersonation.
Motive stems from blackmail and fear of exposure by Neville.

mechanism.description: The culprit, Ferdinand Carrick, disguised himself as Neville Fairweather by wearing a steward’s uniform similar to Neville's usual attire and mimicking his mannerisms on the first-class promenade deck, exploiting the cognitive bias of witnesses who expected to see Neville there. Meanwhile, the real Neville was stabbed in his cabin earlier. To support the deception, Carrick forged Neville’s name in the ship’s engine room logbook to suggest Neville was alive and working during the time of the murder. The torn uniform fabric snagged on the cabin doorframe and the crew schedule contradictions reveal the truth.

delivery_path.step: Carrick dons a steward's uniform identical in style to Neville's usual clothing.
Carrick appears on the first-class promenade deck, where witnesses see him and assume he is Neville.
Carrick forges Neville’s signature in the engine room logbook to provide a false alibi.
The real Neville is stabbed in his cabin before the promenade sighting.

outcome.result: The identity substitution misleads witnesses and investigators until the cognitive bias is exposed, linking Carrick to the murder beyond reasonable doubt.

false_assumption.what_it_hides: That the man seen was actually Ferdinand Carrick impersonating Neville, while the real Neville was already dead in his cabin.

discriminating_test.design: Compare the torn steward uniform fabric found on Neville’s cabin doorframe with authenticated steward uniforms and Neville’s usual clothing fabric under controlled conditions, and examine the engine room logbook ink with forensic analysis already established. The test also reviews crew schedules to confirm who had access to uniforms and logbooks. This directly proves the impersonation and forgery, exposing Ferdinand Carrick’s guilt.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: The test exposes the fabric mismatch and ink forgery, confirming that the man seen on the promenade deck was Carrick in disguise and that the forged logbook entry was created to provide Carrick with an alibi.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: Evidence conclusively links the torn uniform fabric and forged logbook entry to Carrick, eliminating all other suspects.
